The term ""contract"" encompasses a contract, an order, or a project work order. 3.2.2 OVERHAUL: An overhauled part is one which has been disassembled, cleaned, inspected, repaired as necessary (by replacing or repairing all components which have been found to exceed limits established by the repair/overhaul manual) reassembled and tested in accordance with the approved repair/overhaul manual listed in this SOW and returned to a Ready for Issue (RFI) condition (Refer to contract schedule for items to be overhauled). 3.2.3 REPAIR: A repaired part is one which has been restored to a Ready for Issue(RFI) condition (by replacing or repairing those components found to be defective, broken, damaged or inoperative during the initial evaluation and troubleshooting phase) and tested in accordance with the approved repair/overhaul manual listed in this SOW (Refer to contract schedule for items to be repaired). 3.3 3.0 SCOPE 3.3.1 GENERAL. All references to the ""prime contractor"" or the ""actual manufacturer"" appearing on the drawings and / or specifications or technical data furnished by the Government shall be read as the ""Government Designated Agency"" 3.4.3 Process Control Documentation: The contractor shall prepare and maintain repair procedures, and test / inspection information / procedures which shall be made available to the Government for review and approval. The procedures shall include sequential diagrams of processes, as well as the performance specifications to perform the testing / inspection procedures. Those processes shall be frozen after approval of the inspection / Test. 3.4.4 Beyond Economical Repair (BER). An item is BER if the cost of the repair exceeds 75% of the production quantity price to replace the item, current at time of award. This replacement price is for the purposes of BER determinations only, and may not be used or relied on by the offeror in the pricing of the repairs required by this contract. Items determined BER are not included in the contract price. The contractor shall obtain written concurrence from DCMA for all units determined by the contractor to be BER. All such determinations, including the basis for the determination, the repair required, the proposed price to repair and the DCMA written concurrence shall be provided by the contractor to the PCO, with a copy to the inventory manager. After receipt of the required documentation, the PCO shall provide the contractor disposition instructions or contractual authority for repair of the item. The contractor is not authorized to proceed with the repair until notification to proceed is received from the PCO. Any disposal ordered shall be performed by the contractor in accordance with all applicable regulations and in accordance with all DCMA disposal procedures and requirements. 3.4.5 Missing on Induction (MOI). A Weapons Repairable Assembly (WRA) is subject to this MOI provision if the item received by the contractor for repair is missing one or more Shop Replaceable Assemblies (SRAs). Contractor replacement of MOI SRAs is not included in the contract price. The contractor shall immediately notify DCMA when an item is received with MOI SRA(s) and shall obtain written verification from DCMA for all WRAs determined to have MOI SRA(s). The contractor shall provide all such determinations, including identification of the missing SRA(s), and the DCMA written verification, to the Inventory Manager with a copy to the PCO and ACO prior to induction and/or repair of the WRA. The contractor shall not induct and/or repair WRAs with MOI SRAs until instructions on how to proceed are provided to the contractor by the Inventory Manager (where no adjustment price to the contract is required) or by the PCO. Items received by the contractor missing consumable parts are not MOI items. Rather, repair of such items and replacement of the missing consumable parts are included in the contract price and the item shall be inducted and repaired by the contractor under this contract. 3.4.6 Replacing Failed or Missing Shop Replaceable Assembly (SRA) when repairinga Weapons Replaceable Assembly (WRA). 3.4.7 A. When the contractor believes one or more SRA(s) within a WRA are either: 3.4.8 Beyond Economic Repair (BER) or Beyond Repair (BR) i. e. the unit is not capable of being repaired because of the extent of physical damage), or Missing on Induction (MOI), the contractor shall obtain written verification from DCMA and advice from the Inventory Manager whether a SRA may be replaced by one or more of the following options: Ship in place from an existing spares or repair contract, if any, MILSTRIP the SRA(s), otherwise be provided direction for obtaining the SRA(s) at no cost to the contractor.The detailed procedures are set forth in Section 6.0 of the WEB-BASED COMMERCIAL ASSET VISIBILITY (CAV) STATEMENT OF WORK. 3.4.9 B.When not otherwise provided for (or precluded) by other terms of this contract, the contractor may seek written authorization to replace failed SRA(s) with Ready For Issue SRA(s). When authorized, the procedures set forth in paragraph 3.0 of Section 6.2 of the WEB-BASED COMMERCIAL ASSET VISIBILITY (CAV) STATEMENT OF WORK shall be followed. 3.4.10 Over and Above Repair (OAR). An item sent to the contractor shall be considered to require over and above (OAR) repair effort if the repair required is not the type of repair that would be anticipated as a result of normal Navy operation of the item and is not included in the contract pricing due to the nature or scope of the repair needed for that particular item. Therefore, repair of OAR items may be subject to equitable adjustment. The Contractor shall obtain written concurrence from DCMA for all units determined by the contractor to require OAR effort. All such OAR determinations, including the basis for the determination, the repair required, the proposed price to repair and the DCMA written concurrence, shall be provided by the contractor to the PCO prior to undertaking repair of the item. After receipt of the required documentation, the PCO shall provide the contractor disposition instructions or contractual authority for repair of the item. Items determined BER are not included in the contract price. The contractor shall obtain written concurrence from DCMA for all units determined by the contractor to be BER. After receipt of the required documentation, the PCO shall provide the contractor disposition instructions or contractual authority for repair of the item. The contractor is not authorized to proceed with the repair until notification to proceed is received from the PCO. A Weapons Repairable Assembly (WRA) is subject to this MOI provision if the item received by the contractor for repair is missing one or more Shop Replaceable Assemblies (SRAs). Contractor replacement of MOI SRAs is not included in the contract price. The contractor shall immediately notify DCMA when an item is received with MOI SRA(s) and shall obtain written verification from DCMA for all WRAs determined to have MOI SRA(s). The contractor shall provide all such determinations, including identification of the missing SRA(s), and the DCMA written verification, to the Inventory Manager with a copy to the PCO and ACO prior to induction and/or repair of the WRA. The contractor shall not induct and/or repair WRAs with MOI SRAs until instructions on how to proceed are provided to the contractor by the Inventory Manager (where no adjustment price to the contract is required) or by the PCO. Items received by the contractor missing consumable parts are not MOI items. Rather, repair of such items and replacement of the missing consumable parts are included in the contract price and the item shall be inducted and repaired by the contractor under this contract. 3.4.6 Replacing Failed or Missing Shop Replaceable Assembly (SRA) when repairinga Weapons Replaceable Assembly (WRA). 3.4.7 A. In accordance with DoD Instruction (DoDI) 6025.13, Defense Health Agency Procedures Manual (DHA-PM) 6025.13, Air Force Instruction (AFI) 44-119, and DAFMAN 10-211, the scope has modernized to incorporate full clinical quality management and line-side embedded healthcare support. NAVSUP WSS Code N2 has determined that the requirements at DFARS 211.274 which mandates the use of DFARS clause 252.211-7003 ""Item Unique Identification and Valuation"" in all solicitations and contracts, be deleted from all non-CLSSA FMS spares requirements processed by NAVSUP WSS and DLA-Aviation. The affected parts are wholly owned by FMS customer countries, are not covered by a Cooperative Logistics Supply Support Arrangement (CLSSA), these same assets will be delivered to the customer country for their sole use. The IUID definition at DFARS 211.274-1 says IUID ""is a system of marking, valuing and tracking items delivered to DoD."" These spares are non-CLSSA FMS assets and will never be delivered to DoD. The assets are delivered to a domestic U.S. freight forwarder who is under contract by the FMS customer to ship the assets to the country of record. The FMS customer countries retain ownership of their parts throughout the asset's lifecycle. These parts will never be owned by the U.S. Government, and will never be entered into the DoD supply chain. Based on this, there is no need for these non-CLSSA FMS country assets to be specially marked for tracking by DoD. \"

(end update) The Army Contracting Command – Rock Island (ACC-RI), on behalf of Project Manage, Close Combat Systems (PM CCS), is providing information to industry regarding the Grenade, Hand Fragmentation Delay M67 (M67 Fragmentation Hand Grenade), Grenade, Hand: Offensive, M111 (M111 Offensive Hand Grenade), and Body, Practice Hand Grenade: Offensive, M112 (M112 Practice Offensive Hand Grenade Body). The purpose of providing this information is to conduct ongoing market research and to identify interested sources capable of manufacturing and delivering the following items: GRENADE, HAND FRAGMENTATION DELAY M67 (M67 Fragmentation Hand Grenade), NSN: 1330-01-563-0592, DODIC: G881, Top Level Drawing: 9235492, Specification: MIL-DTL-14933. The M67 Fragmentation Hand Grenade produces casualties by high velocity projection of fragments in a uniform pattern when detonated. The M67 utilizes a steel spherical body filled with high explosives that are initiated by a pyrotechnic delay fuze. This device is comprised of three (3) major components: 1) the metal body, 2) a pyrotechnic delay detonating fuze, and 3) the Load, Assemble and Pack (LAP) of the explosive composition and the components into the final assembly. The final assembly utilizes military packaging (fiber tube (individual grenade) and wooden overpack). GRENADE, HAND: OFFENSIVE, M111 (M111 Offensive Hand Grenade), NSN: 1330-01-648-9824, DODIC: GG37, Top Level Drawing: 13068375, Specification: MIL-DTL-32581. The M111 Offensive Hand Grenade is designed to produce casualties during close combat while minimizing danger to friendly personnel. The grenade is used for concussive effects in enclosed areas. The M111 produces a shock wave, known as blast overpressure, in enclosed areas greater than those produced by the lethal M67 Fragmentation Hand Grenade during detonation. Therefore, it is very effective against enemy soldiers located in bunkers, buildings, and fortified areas. The output couples a bright flash, loud explosion, and enhanced blast overpressure. BODY, PRACTICE HAND GRENADE: OFFENSIVE, M112 (M112 Practice Offensive Hand Grenade Body), NSN: 1330-01-651-4358, DODIC: GG38, Top Level Drawing: 13068386, Specification: MIL-DTL-32580. The M112 Practice Offensive Hand Grenade Body with M228 Practice Fuze is a reloadable trainer. The M112 body is intended to replicate the size, shape, and weight (minus the fuze weight), and markings of the M111. Responses: 1. (end update) The Army Contracting Command – Rock Island (ACC-RI), on behalf of Project Manage, Close Combat Systems (PM CCS), is providing information to industry regarding the Grenade, Hand Fragmentation Delay M67 (M67 Fragmentation Hand Grenade), Grenade, Hand: Offensive, M111 (M111 Offensive Hand Grenade), and Body, Practice Hand Grenade: Offensive, M112 (M112 Practice Offensive Hand Grenade Body). The purpose of providing this information is to conduct ongoing market research and to identify interested sources capable of manufacturing and delivering the following items: GRENADE, HAND FRAGMENTATION DELAY M67 (M67 Fragmentation Hand Grenade), NSN: 1330-01-563-0592, DODIC: G881, Top Level Drawing: 9235492, Specification: MIL-DTL-14933. The M67 Fragmentation Hand Grenade produces casualties by high velocity projection of fragments in a uniform pattern when detonated. The M67 utilizes a steel spherical body filled with high explosives that are initiated by a pyrotechnic delay fuze. This device is comprised of three (3) major components: 1) the metal body, 2) a pyrotechnic delay detonating fuze, and 3) the Load, Assemble and Pack (LAP) of the explosive composition and the components into the final assembly. The final assembly utilizes military packaging (fiber tube (individual grenade) and wooden overpack). GRENADE, HAND: OFFENSIVE, M111 (M111 Offensive Hand Grenade), NSN: 1330-01-648-9824, DODIC: GG37, Top Level Drawing: 13068375, Specification: MIL-DTL-32581. The M111 Offensive Hand Grenade is designed to produce casualties during close combat while minimizing danger to friendly personnel. The grenade is used for concussive effects in enclosed areas. The M111 produces a shock wave, known as blast overpressure, in enclosed areas greater than those produced by the lethal M67 Fragmentation Hand Grenade during detonation. Therefore, it is very effective against enemy soldiers located in bunkers, buildings, and fortified areas. The output couples a bright flash, loud explosion, and enhanced blast overpressure. BODY, PRACTICE HAND GRENADE: OFFENSIVE, M112 (M112 Practice Offensive Hand Grenade Body), NSN: 1330-01-651-4358, DODIC: GG38, Top Level Drawing: 13068386, Specification: MIL-DTL-32580. The M112 Practice Offensive Hand Grenade Body with M228 Practice Fuze is a reloadable trainer. The M112 body is intended to replicate the size, shape, and weight (minus the fuze weight), and markings of the M111. Responses: 1. There are currently no known design issues that would preclude the M111 from achieving full materiel release and transition into full rate production. However, there is a known risk related to the M111’s energetic fill (PAX-3 high explosive). One constituent of the energetic fill, the BDNPAF binder, has limited sources of supply. A contractor’s inability to source this binder to produce the energetic fill or ultimately source the energetic fill required to produce the M111 may be experienced. The Government does not intend to provide the energetic fill as Government Furnished Material (GFM). Respondents should provide detailed information related to sourcing the constituent materials and ultimately the energetic fill for the M111. 8. General Information This combined synopsis/solicitation is issued by Army Contracting Command - APG - Orlando Division to procure Agile Professional Services (""APS""). The acquisition is structured to support critical technical and professional operations under a flexible framework, to be proposed and developed by the successful offeror. Solicitation Details This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; proposals are being requested and a written solicitation will not be issued. This combined synopsis/solicitation is prepared in accordance with the format in FAR Subpart 12.6, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. The solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular FAC 2025-06, effective August 27, 2025.and DFARS Publication Notice (DPN) July 2, 2026. As described in the attached FAR 52.212-2, The Army will adopt aspects of FAR Part 15 evaluation procedures. Considering the novel, and commercial, nature of these services this is deemed necessary to balance fairness, transparency, and competition with the interests of expediency and flexibility 3. Description of Requirement CPE ST3 has a need for Agile Professional Services (APS) support services to provide the organization with the ability to augment its Military and Government Civilian workforce in order to execute its mission. The services will be limited to providing professional support services, under a Performance Based Services model, to CPE ST3 and CPE ST3 customers for limited requirements which are related to CPE ST3’s mission. Since its inception, CPE ST3 has relied on contractor support to conduct its mission in all phases of life cycle management due to insufficient personnel within the organization to successfully perform the required services. This model of a Government footprint with a scalable contractor workforce has enabled CPE ST3 to be very flexible and agile in its mission to support the changing needs of the Army. The services to be performed will include related activities in support of all aspects of providing responsive integrated and interoperable infrastructure for simulation, training, testing, and threat solutions. APS support services are required for effective, efficient, and responsive full lifecycle management of efforts to include, but not limited to: vision statements and doctrine, development of architectures, program support (e.g., acquisition and budget planning, business and financial programming and execution, modeling, simulation, simulator, training device, and instrumentation development, documentation, fielding and execution, system analysis and integration, integrated logistics support, strategic planning, contingency and mission support, security cooperation/international relations, program oversight, independent verification validation and test evaluation, prototype development, sustainment and operations, and analysis of emerging technologies support), and subject matter experts on military tactics, techniques, and procedures. Potential areas of growth are envisioned but not limited to be in the areas of Cyber and Information Warfare, Robotics, Unmanned Vehicles, Home Station Training, Multi-Sensory Simulation, Artificial Intelligence, Hypersonics, Directed Energy, Electronic Warfare, Autonomous Systems, Multi-Domain Integration, Target and Threat Systems, Environment Modeling, Human Performance Training, Security Cooperation, Nuclear Engineering, and Medical Training. The critical performance requirement is the successful development and transition of CPE ST3 from a traditional, staffing-based support model to a task-based, outcome-driven Agile delivery framework that is to be developed by the Performer. Success will be measured by the contractor's ability to develop and iterate, through performance under the resultant contract, a framework that both provides the following, and is able to be replicated across future requirements. 4. NAICS Code: 236220 – Commercial and Institutional Building Construction (Note: While Other Transaction Authority is not subject to FAR-based small business regulations, this NAICS code is provided for market research to help the Government understand the size and demographics of the interested industrial base.) Small Business Size Standard: $45 Million PROJECT OVERVIEW The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Alaska District, has a requirement for the site-wide repair and replacement of fire alarm systems at Eareckson Air Station (Shemya Island, Alaska). The project will replace aging and non-compliant fire alarm systems across multiple facilities to meet current UFC 3-600-01, NFPA 72, and life-safety requirements. Existing systems are outdated or non-functional, creating risk to personnel and mission on this remote installation. The Government is now pursuing a wireless (or hybrid wireless) fire alarm architecture that significantly reduces or eliminates the need for extensive buried fiber optic infrastructure, thereby addressing the primary cost driver while achieving full code compliance. Key project components include: • Demolition of existing fire alarm control panels, initiating devices, notification appliances, conduit, and wiring across affected buildings • Installation of a new wireless/hybrid addressable fire alarm system, including wireless devices, gateways/repeaters for campus-wide RF coverage, limited residual hard-wired elements only where essential, and integration with supervisory/monitoring capabilities • RF coverage analysis, specialty detection in hazardous (Class I) locations associated with fuel systems, cybersecurity compliance, multi-shift training, testing, commissioning, and phased turnover • Phased execution by building or geographic area to accommodate remote-island logistics and minimize operational impact Estimated Acquisition Magnitude: Between $27M and $33M Planned Acquisition Strategy: Anticipated to utilize Progressive Design Build via Other Transaction Authority (OTA) The Alaska District is conducting market intelligence to assess industry capability and interest in supporting this effort utilizing an Other Transaction (OT) Agreement under the authority of 10 U.S.C. § 2808a, Facility Construction or Repair: Transactions Other Than Contracts and Grants. This authority is distinct from the Department of Defense prototype OT authorities commonly associated with 10 U.S.C. § 4021 and 4022. This authority is intended for military construction and repair projects that involve testing and experimentation associated with new and emergent construction technologies to achieve potential benefits such as enhanced mission resilience, improved installation support, or cost and schedule reduction. The anticipated delivery method is Progressive Design-Build. Design and Pre-Construction Services - The OT Awardee shall assist the Government collaboratively in advancing the wireless/hybrid fire alarm design, performing RF coverage analysis and site investigations, supporting the UFC waiver process, validating and refining project requirements, and developing progressively more detailed open-book cost and schedule information. Design is expected to advance from approximately 0–15% at award to an agreed interim milestone (target approximately 65%) sufficient for reliable Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP) development. Final Design and Construction - Upon reaching an agreed-upon level of design, the Awardee will propose a Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP) or Firm-Fixed-Price for final design and construction. If the price is accepted and required funding/approvals (including UFC waiver status) are in place, the Government will authorize Phase 2 execution via modification. Construction is expected to be authorized in staggered packages by building or geographic area to allow early turnover of priority facilities. If a fair and reasonable price cannot be agreed upon, or if other conditions prevent proceeding, the Government retains an “off-ramp” to complete the project via alternative methods while retaining rights to the design developed during Phase 1. PROJECT BACKGROUND The Sentinel (Ground Based Strategic Deterrent) program is modernizing the Nation’s land-based intercontinental ballistic missile force. At Malmstrom AFB, the Air Force is constructing a suite of new facilities collectively referred to as the Operations and Maintenance Complex (OMC), together with associated support facilities. The Utility Infrastructure Project is the critical enabling backbone that must be in place before the remaining Sentinel facilities can be constructed and made operational. Scope of the Utility Infrastructure Improvements project includes construction of a comprehensive utilities distribution system serving the entire Sentinel GBSD Complex at Malmstrom AFB. Primary elements include: Electrical distribution systems, including connection to / expansion of electrical substation capacity as required to serve the new campus. Water distribution and related appurtenances. Wastewater collection and connection to treatment systems. Natural gas service to the campus. Telecommunications backbone connectivity, including fiber services to Information Transfer Nodes (ITNs), electrical substation, water pump stations, and related Base utility facilities. Associated site work: clearing, grubbing, grading, minor demolition, drainage, utility and communications connections, access paving, parking, and walkways as applicable. Additional Information: Please note that this special notice relates to previously issued Special Notice ID “W912DW26S1CE0” titled, ""Request for Information - Sentinel Utility Infrastructure, Malmstrom Air Force Base, MT"" Note: This is an Industry Day notice only. This notice is solely for informational purposes regarding an upcoming industry day and should not be construed as a request for offers or proposals. The Government is not committed to issuing a solicitation or awarding an agreement based on this notice."

The Government does not guarantee any minimum quantity of propane or minimum number of calls. Small Business Size Standard: $45 Million PROJECT OVERVIEW The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Louisville District, has a requirement for the design and construction of a project to restore and modernize the potable water system and wastewater collection system throughout the Fort Hunter Liggett Installation. The scope of work consists of furnishing all necessary design services, equipment, materials, labor, construction management, supervision, quality control, and supplies to deliver a fully functional and modernized potable water and wastewater systems on the Installation. The Fort Hunter Liggett water distribution system dates back to the 1950’s with a few areas believed to be even older and includes a three (3) well configuration that has sufficient pumping capacity to serve current supply demands, however, the water transmission system is undersized to satisfy the demand of the system. While the current water system storage may be sufficient for normal operation, it cannot sustain the system for more than one day in the event of a pump outage and/or fire flow event during maximum day conditions; therefore, additional system storage is necessary. A new Tank Farm with adequate storage capacity (estimated to be a minimum of 2 million gallons) to be determined and validated in accordance with NSPC, UFC, and NFPA criteria, should be in vicinity of security fence gate 10 (Lat: 35.997638° , Long: -121.224355°). Currently the primary storage tank for the potable water system is on the opposite side of the cantonment from the wells and the transmission main and distribution are combined causing significant pressure variations far in excess of industry standard, causing accelerated deterioration of system components. Many pipelines, valves, and hydrants within the distribution system have currently exceeded their useful life expectancy and have failed or failing. High operating pressures place additional strain on this aging system, requiring operational improvements as well as rehabilitation/replacement of existing assets. Modernizing SCADA components are necessary to increase efficiency and updated to cover any system revisions and future improvements. SCADA infrastructure improvements shall integrate into the existing SCADA infrastructure. Fort Hunter Liggett’s wastewater collection system was installed around the same time as the water potable system. Due to the age of the system and deterioration, replacement and rehabilitation of sanitary sewer lines, manholes, and the waste treatment plant lagoon are needed to return the system to be fully functional and code compliant. The wastewater treatment plant relies on a series of lagoons to treat sewage. There are lagoons that have operational deficiencies and require the replacement of the impermeable liner. In addition, the lagoon currently lacks baffles, which are essential for directing the flow of wastewater in a way that maximizes treatment time and prevents ""short circuiting"". Estimated Acquisition Magnitude: $70-$80M PRIMARY ACQUISITION STRATEGY UNDER EVALUATION: Progressive Design Build (PDB) via Other Transaction Authority (OTA). The Louisville District is evaluating a Progressive Design Build (PDB) strategy utilizing an Other Transaction (OT) Agreement under the authority of 10 U.S.C. § 2808a. This authority authorizes transactions other than standard contracts to carry out facility repair and construction projects – including planning, design, engineering, piloting and execution – enabling early contractor involvement, commercial pricing transparency, and schedule and cost efficiencies. Currently, the Government has advanced a conceptual design for the following potable water system features below. New transmission main to connect the existing well field to the main distribution system within the cantonment area. New storage infrastructure as required to satisfy requirements for fire safety, emergency needs, and operational storage. Upgrades to existing water supply wells to enhance water-supply reliability and redundancy. A Technical Assessment Report of the condition of Fort Hunter Liggett’s utilities systems and modernization recommendations of the water and sanitary sewer systems was completed in June 2024. The onsite assessments used in developing the Technical Assessment Report were conducted November 28-December 7, 2023. Therefore, the Government is utilizing this RFI to assess industry capability, interest, and the advantages of utilizing PDB utilizing an OT Agreement under the authority of 10 U.S.C. § 2808a. The PDB Course of Action (10 U.S.C. § 2808a): The evaluation process for selection of the most highly qualified design-builder would be qualifications based. A streamlined, two-step Qualifications-Based Selection would occur: Step 1: White Papers/Statement of Qualifications submission. Step 2: Down selected design builders would be invited to Pitch Meetings/Presentations. Most highly qualified firm following pitch meetings would be selected to enter into negotiations. The OT Award would be two phases: Phase 1 (Design & Pre-Construction): The Government team will negotiate the price of Agreement Phase I – Design and Pre-Construction Services with the selected design-builder. work collaboratively to advance the design, conduct open-book cost estimating, and mitigate project risks. Phase 2 (Construction): Upon reaching an agreed-upon level of design (e.g., 60% to 90%), the Awardee will propose a Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP). If the GMP is accepted, the Government will exercise Phase 2 for construction execution. If a GMP cannot be agreed upon, the Government retains an ""off-ramp"" to complete the design and construct the facility via alternative methods INFORMATION REQUESTED Interested parties are requested to respond to the following questions to help shape the final acquisition strategy. THE OPPORTUNITY The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Far East District (USACE FED) invites industry partners to help shape the acquisition strategy for a high-priority modernization and sustainment program involving ICD-705 controlled spaces at Osan Air Base, Republic of Korea. The Government is evaluating an innovative Progressive Design-Build (PDB) delivery method executed through an Other Transaction Agreement (OTA) under 10 U.S.C. § 2808a. This approach enables early contractor involvement, collaborative design development, open-book pricing, and flexible risk allocation—advantages particularly valuable for complex, security-sensitive work performed in an active overseas operational environment with unique host-nation and ICD-705 constraints. The Government has not made a final acquisition strategy determination and seeks candid industry input on the benefits, limitations, risks, and commercial terms of a PDB OTA compared with traditional design-bid-build or design-build approaches. WHY PROGRESSIVE DESIGN-BUILD / OTA? ICD-705 controlled spaces, collective protection systems, and HVAC modernization on an active air base present technical, security, operational, and logistical complexities that benefit from early industry engagement. A PDB OTA structure may allow: Joint refinement of requirements and design while the facility remains operational; Early identification and mitigation of long-lead items, host-nation interfaces, and ICD-705 accreditation risks; Transparent, open-book cost development leading to a more reliable construction baseline (including potential GMP); Flexible commercial terms and governance tailored to the unique constraints of overseas military construction in the Republic of Korea. The Government is particularly interested in industry’s practical experience with these methods on similar secure or operationally constrained projects, as well as any recommended alternatives that would better achieve mission, schedule, and cost objectives. PROJECT SCOPE The program encompasses modernization and sustainment work in two existing facilities at Osan Air Base: Building A – Collective Protection, HVAC & ICD-705 Modernization Replace the existing M49 Collective Protection System (CPS) filter system with a new M98 CPS, including associated blast doors, seals, relief valves, electronic control systems, and other appurtenances, fully coordinated with applicable ICD-705 requirements. Replace or modernize principal components of the existing HVAC system to support ICD-705 environmental and security standards. Convert approximately 2,610 square feet of existing space to meet applicable ICD-705 requirements. Building B – ICD-705 Conversion & Facility Sustainment Convert approximately 3,700 square feet of existing space to meet applicable ICD-705 requirements. Perform sustainment work on approximately 50,000 square feet, including roof repairs and existing office space improvements. Repair and/or replace components of the existing fire protection and fire alarm systems; air-handling units (AHUs), air-cooled condensing units (ACCUs), and associated HVAC infrastructure; bathroom fixtures and plumbing; plus associated incidental work required to complete the planned improvements. Estimated program magnitude: $60–100 million. Construction funding for both facilities is anticipated for obligation in FY27, subject to availability of funds and applicable approvals. This Sources Sought is the Government’s primary tool to assess industry interest, capability, and preferred commercial practices before finalizing the acquisition approach. ACQUISITION APPROACH UNDER EVALUATION Industry feedback will help refine potential agreement structure, project phasing, pricing approach, governance, risk allocation, and other commercial terms. Potential Phase 1 – Design and Preconstruction The Government and selected contractor would collaborate to refine project requirements, develop the design, conduct constructability reviews, identify long-lead equipment, evaluate phasing and operational constraints, obtain subcontractor input, develop cost estimates, and mitigate technical and execution risks. Feedback is requested on the design maturity, site investigations, pricing information, and agreement terms needed to establish a reliable construction cost and schedule baseline. Potential Phase 2 – Construction Following design development and resolution of key technical and commercial risks, the contractor may be asked to propose a construction price, potentially including a Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP) if appropriate to the final structure. Any transition to construction would be subject to the terms of the resulting agreement, Government acceptance, availability of funds, and required approvals. The Government seeks practical recommendations for off-ramp provisions, design deliverables, compensation, and transition arrangements should the parties be unable to reach agreement on construction pricing or other required terms. Alternative acquisition strategies that industry believes would better support the program’s security, technical, schedule, cost, and operational requirements are welcome and encouraged. Basis for Award ""The Government will award a Firm-Fixed-Price contract resulting from this solicitation to the responsible offeror whose quote conforms to the solicitation requirements and represents the Lowest Price Technically Acceptable (LPTA) to the Government. Award will be made on an 'all or none' basis to the lowest-priced, technically acceptable offeror. Tradeoffs will not be permitted. Quotes will be evaluated for technical acceptability, past performance acceptability, and price."" Evaluation Process: ""The Government intends to evaluate quotes by first sorting them from lowest price to highest price. The lowest-priced quote will then be evaluated for technical acceptability and past performance. If the lowest-priced quote is determined to be 'Technically Acceptable' and has 'Acceptable Past Performance,' award will be made to that offeror, and no further quotes will be evaluated."" Factor 1: Technical Acceptability: ""The technical quote will be evaluated on a pass/fail basis. To be rated Acceptable, the quote must clearly demonstrate a compliance approach that meets all requirements outlined in the Performance Work Statement (PWS), specifically demonstrating the capability to distribute media across the required channels and networks."" Factor 2: Past Performance: ""Past Performance will be evaluated on an Acceptable/Unacceptable basis. To be rated Acceptable, the offeror must submit a minimum of two (2) references within the past three (3) years demonstrating similar scope, complexity, and NAICS 311991 relevance. Offerors with no relevant past performance history will receive a 'Neutral' rating, which will be treated as 'Acceptable' for award purposes."" Factor 3: Price: ""Price will be evaluated for mathematical completeness and price reasonableness. Award will be made to the lowest total priced, responsible offeror whose technical and past performance quotes are rated Acceptable."" Performance Work Statement 1.0 SCOPE This Statement of Work (SOW) outlines the requirements for a non-personal services contract to provide complete dining facility (DFAC) and meal services for the United States Army. The Contractor shall provide all necessary personnel, equipment, tools, materials, supervision, and quality control to perform the full scope of food services as defined herein, with the exception of government-furnished property and services. 2.0 GENERAL REQUIREMENTS The Contractor shall perform complete food services and meet the performance standards set forth in this document. All services will be performed in strict accordance with all applicable local, county, state, and federal regulations, as well as military-specific guidelines, including but not limited to the Tri-Service Food Code (TB MED 530) and Army Regulation (AR) 30-22. Contract can be terminated if it is determined to not meet the needs of the Military unit being serviced. 2.1 Pricing and Payment Terms: The contractor shall provide a detailed pricing structure based on the following: • Cost per meal (breakfast, lunch, dinner). • Total meal count per day will vairy throughout the course (see Annex A) • Payment terms (e.g., weekly invoicing, net 30 days). 3.0 COORDINATION AND LOGISTICS 3.1 Adherence to Meal and Strength Schedule: The Government will provide a Meal Service and Strength Schedule (attached as Annex A). This schedule will detail the required mealtimes and the exact personnel count for each meal service (breakfast, lunch, and dinner) for the entire period of performance. The Contractor must strictly adhere to the specified times and headcounts listed in this schedule for all meal preparations and deliveries. The final invoice must match the numbers specified in this calendar. Any deviation not pre-approved in writing may result in non-payment for the excess meals provided. Delivery times for meals are referenced in Annex A 169th RTI 1st Quarter Course Meal Plan FY27. The timeline for meals is as follows unless otherwise annotated: Breakfast: 0700-0800, Lunch 1200-1245, Dinner 1700-1745. 3.2 Meal Order Modifications: All requests for changes to meal quantities or meal types must be submitted by the designated Government Point of Contact (POC) to the contractor via email or text message. No changes will be accepted by the contractor any later than 72 hours prior to the scheduled meal delivery time. This 72-hour deadline is firm and ensures the contractor has adequate time for procurement and preparation. The contractor is not obligated to accommodate requests made after this deadline. 3.3 Singular Drop-off Location: All meals shall be delivered to a single, designated delivery point. The specific location will be the main dining facility at the regional training institute, the address for which will be provided upon contract award. Under no circumstances shall the contractor deliver meals to any other location, including field training sites or administrative offices, unless explicitly directed in writing by the Contracting Officer (CO) or the designated Government Point of Contact (POC). The contractor is responsible for all transportation to the designated location. 3.4 Delivery Timeliness and Notification: Punctuality of meal delivery is critical. The Contractor must ensure all meal deliveries are made within a five-minute window of the agreed-upon delivery time (no earlier than five minutes before and no later than five minutes after the scheduled time). In the event of an unavoidable delay that will result in a late delivery, the Contractor shall immediately notify the designated Government schoolhouse Point of Contact (POC) by telephone. Contact information for this POC will be provided upon contract award. 4.0 HOLIDAY SERVICES 4.1 Meal services may be required on Federal and State holidays. It is the responsibility of the Contracting Officer's Representative (COR) to notify the Contractor at least one (1) week in advance of any holidays that require meal services. 4.2 A list of recognized holidays applicable to this contract will be provided by the Government upon award. If a holiday occurs on a Saturday, the Government may observe it on the preceding Friday. If a holiday occurs on a Sunday, the Government may observe it on the following Monday. The Contractor shall provide services on the observed day as directed. 5.0 MEAL SERVICE AND SERVING REQUIREMENTS 5.1 Standard Meal Service: For standard daily meals, the Contractor shall be responsible for the preparation, delivery, and service of breakfast, lunch, and dinner, utilizing using a packaged meal service. The Contractor shall provide all meals individually packaged for single serve/ single use consumption. Each delivery must be clearly labeled with the contents, date of preparation, and any relevant dietary information. All packaging must be suitable for maintaining required food-safe temperatures (hot or cold) and preventing spillage or contamination during transport and distribution. 5.2 Boxed Lunches: Upon request by the Government, the Contractor shall assemble and provide boxed lunches for delivery on an as-needed basis. It is the responsibility of the COR to notify the Contractor in writing at least forty-eight (48) hours in advance of when boxed lunch meals are required. The contents of the boxed lunches shall be agreed upon by both parties prior to the first order. Hot or boxed meals will be outlined by date and meal in Annex A 169th RTI 1st Quarter Course Meal Plan FY27 5.3 The Contractor shall provide and maintain two complete sets of all necessary non-disposable delivery equipment. This includes, but is not limited to, insulated food transport containers. One set of equipment will be used for the delivery of a meal service. The Government will make this used set available for collection upon completion of the meal service. The Contractor is responsible for retrieving the used equipment, typically at the time of the next scheduled meal delivery, at which point the second, clean equipment will be dropped off. This rotation ensures one set of equipment is always on-site while the other is with the Contractor for cleaning and preparation. 6.0 MENU AND MEAL PLANNING 6.1 The provided 35 Day Menu FY 2027 (attached as Annex B) shall be utilized as a reference and basis for developing menu cycles. While the exact menu is not mandatory, the variety, quality, and types of items offered must be of a comparable standard. A sample 14-day menu from the Contractor will be provided to the COR or POC prior to awarding the contract. 6.2 At a minimum, each meal service shall include: - Breakfast: A minimum of one non-pork meat option, eggs, one (1) hot starch (e.g., potatoes), assorted fresh fruits, whole grain bread/pastry options, and assorted beverages (coffee, tea, juice, milk). “Continental breakfast” option only on the last day of the scheduled course. - Lunch & Dinner: Should include one hot entrée (two if the main entrée is pork, one of which shall be a non-pork option if pork is served), one (1) starch, one (1) cooked vegetable, a prepared salad option, fresh fruit, and assorted beverages. 7.0 DIETARY RESTRICTIONS AND SPECIAL MEALS 7.1 The Contractor must be prepared to accommodate common and specific dietary needs. A vegetarian and/or vegan entrée option shall be available at every breakfast, lunch and dinner service. Meals for students with dietary restrictions will be clearly labeled to prevent confusion. 7.2 The Contractor shall have the capability to make immediate or near-immediate changes to meal preparations to accommodate the dietary restrictions of students or staff upon their arrival. This includes, but is not limited to, food allergies (e.g., nut, dairy, gluten), religious dietary requirements, and other medical necessities. The Government Point of Contact will provide notification of these requirements as they are identified. 8.0 HEALTH, SANITATION, AND QUALITY CONTROL 8.1 The Contractor shall develop and maintain an effective Quality Control Plan (QCP) to ensure all services are performed in accordance with this PWS. The QCP shall be submitted for Government approval within five (5) business days of contract award. 8.2 Contractor Self-Inspections: The Contractor shall conduct its own on-site quality inspections of delivered food. At a minimum, one meal service shall be inspected upon delivery per week. These inspections will verify food quality, correct temperature, packaging integrity, and adherence to the approved menu. The Contractor must maintain an inspection log detailing the date, time, findings, and any corrective actions taken. This log shall be made available to the COR upon request. 8.3 All food shall be prepared, stored, and transported in a manner that prevents foodborne illness. All food contact surfaces, storage containers, and delivery vehicles must be maintained in a clean and sanitary condition. 8.4 The Government reserves the right to inspect the Contractor's facilities, equipment, and processes at any time to ensure compliance with all health, sanitation, and performance standards. 9. Acceptance Criteria: The contracting organization will evaluate the contractor's performance based on: timely delivery of meals, quality and freshness of meals, and adherence to dietary requirements. 10. Termination Clause: The contracting organization reserves the right to terminate the contract if the contractor fails to meet the requirements outlined in this SOW. Delivery, Logistics, & Temperature Control 1.1 MEAL DELIVERY & TEMPERATURE INTEGRITY The Contractor shall deliver all meals to the designated site no later than thirty (30) minutes and no earlier than forty-five (45) minutes prior to the scheduled mess hour. 1.2 TEMPERATURE MAINTENANCE Hot meals must arrive and be maintained at an internal temperature of no less than 135°F (57°C) throughout the entire service period. Cold meals must be maintained at or below 41°F (5°C). The Contractor shall provide all necessary insulated food carriers (e.g., Cambros) to guarantee these temperature thresholds. 1.3 UNAUTHORIZED MENU SUBSTITUTION Under no circumstances shall the Contractor substitute a scheduled hot meal for a cold meal, or alter the approved menu, without prior written approval from the Contracting Officer (KO) or COR at least 48 hours in advance. Failure to obtain written approval for menu swaps will result in a non-conformance penalty. The determination to conduct a competitive procurement based on responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Contracting Officer PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT Personalized Interventions for Traumatic Brain Injury and Posttraumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD) INTRODUCTION: The mission of VA s National Center for PTSD (NCPTSD) is to advance the clinical care and social welfare of America's Veterans and others who have experienced trauma, or who suffer from PTSD, through research, education, and training in the science, diagnosis, and treatment of PTSD and stress-related disorders. We generate, collate, synthesize, disseminate, and promote implementation of the best information about PTSD. SCOPE: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) and PTSD are significant problems for Veterans and can lead to neuropsychiatric symptoms that pose extensive quality of life burdens on affected individuals. These conditions share similar pathology, and thus, there is a growing interest in developing treatments that target shared mechanisms. Disrupted communication between brain regions is one mechanism thought to perpetuate symptomatology. To guide personalized interventions, there is a critical need to define neural signatures that are associated with behavioral domains of impairment and response to treatment. Using models, the current project will evaluate neural signatures and behavioral deficits following exposure to neurotrauma or psychological trauma. Targeted treatment (brain stimulation, pharmacotherapy, or combination) will then be administered to improve outcomes. The proposed work supports ongoing collaborative research conducted by investigators at the White River Junction VA. Key activities to be performed include: 1) Define behavioral deficits, 2) Define neural signatures, and 3) Define treatment outcomes. PERIOD AND PLACE OF PERFORMANCE: This contract anticipates service utilization that will occur over the course of five years. The place of performance will be at both the White River Junction VA Healthcare System (WRJ-VAHS) and the contractor location, Mary Hitchcock Memorial Hospital for itself and on behalf of Dartmouth-Hitchcock Clinic (MHMH/DHC). Approximately 25% of the work will be performed at the WRJ-VAHS, and the other 75% of work will be performed in Dr. Wilder Doucette s laboratory at MHMH/DHC. The contract location is located within a 30-minute drive of the WRJ facility to ease transportation of the subjects. It has been determined that transportation can be feasibility performed, due to shared veterinary resource agreement between locations. PROJECT MANAGEMENT AND STAFFING: Wilder Doucette, MD, PhD (Project Lead). Dr. Doucette is a Research Affiliate (WOC) at the WRJ-VAHS and Assistant Professor of Psychiatry and Program Director of the Psychiatry Residency Research Track at the Geisel School of Medicine. His research focuses on the systems-level neural activity underpinnings of behavior and how neuromodulation-based treatments alter this activity and improve dysfunction. His research-informed, part-time clinical practice focuses on interventional and addiction psychiatry, and he has extensive experience with pre-clinical models of neuropsychiatric deficits. Dr. Doucette has experience with pre-clinical interventions, including brain stimulation and targeted pharmacotherapy, and using assays to define neurobehavioral deficits in clinically relevant models of psychiatric illness. Dr. Doucette will be responsible for overseeing the behavioral assessments, treatment, and brain activity recording for the current project. Dr. Doucette will be involved in data analyses, interpretation of findings and helping to prepare results for dissemination and publication. Elise Bragg, BS, RLATG, Senior Research Associate (WOC). Mrs. Bragg is Dr. Doucette s Lab Manager at MHMH/DHC. She has extensive pre-clinical experience, including neuromodulation and performing neurobehavioral assessments in subjects, and holds a Registered Laboratory Technologist (RLATG) designation by the American Association for Laboratory Animal Science (AALAS). Mrs. Bragg will be responsible for the stress induction, behavioral assays, treatment, and electrophysiologic measures proposed in the current study and overseeing the preparation of study subjects for surgery. TBD, graduate Student(s). Dr. Doucette s lab is a training site for various undergraduate, graduate, and medical students, as well as post-doctoral fellows. Under Dr. Doucette and Mrs. Bragg s mentorship and oversight, students will assist with pre- and post-operative care, stress and injury induction, and behavioral testing. Additionally, they will provide data entry and other administrative support to the project. BACKGROUND: The WRJ Translational Neuroscience Research Group aims to identify and evaluate novel interventions for TBI and PTSD. Using models, the current project aims to determine how targeted treatment can be used to alter behavioral deficits associated with neurotrauma and psychological trauma. Validated pre-clinical behavioral assays will be used to assess impairment. Brain stimulation will be delivered via customized electrodes targeting clinically relevant brain regions, and pharmacotherapy will be administered to target underlying mechanisms of brain stimulation or enhance treatment response. Neural activity biomarkers will be collected to assess how systems-level brain activity relates to behavioral deficits and response to treatment. Subjects will be assessed at various time points throughout the study. PERFORMANCE OBJECTIVES/DELIVERY SCHEDULE: Define behavioral deficits associated with neurotrauma or trauma exposure (deliver data set and report within 6 months of contract start date). Determine the utility of neural activity biomarkers to identify subjects with behavioral deficits or personalize treatment (deliver data set and report within 6 months of contract start date). Determine the utility of neuromodulation and targeted pharmacotherapy to improve behavioral deficits (deliver data set and report within 9 months of contract start date). Summarize study findings (deliver data set and report within 12 months of contract start date) and there after. Acceptable completion of deliverables will be determined through receipt of complete data sets that include details of all procedures, behavioral outcomes, and statistical comparisons. All deliverables include estimated personnel and supply costs associated with planned studies. OPERATING CONSTRAINTS: Subjects will be randomly assigned to study conditions, which include naÃ¯ves, TBI/Sham injury, Trauma/Sham exposure, and Active/Sham treatment. Shockwave-induced brain injuries will be administered with a blast tube (ORA, Inc.) located at the WRJ-VAHS according to published protocols. Psychological trauma (PTSD-induction) will be experimentally induced according to published protocols, which include but are not limited to the inescapable shock or single-prolonged stress models. Behavioral assays will be conducted to assess clinically-relevant domains of impairment according to published protocols. Brain stimulation. Custom-built electrode arrays will be implanted using stereotactic surgery targeting brain regions, which include but are not limited to the infralimbic cortex, prelimbic cortex, nucleus accumbens core, and the central nucleus of the amygdala. Pharmacotherapy will be administered to target underlying mechanisms of brain stimulation or enhance treatment response. Neural signatures. Electrophysiological measures (i.e., local field potentials) will be recorded from brain regions with and without treatment. PUBLICATION/COLLABORATION ON RESULTS: Intellectual property rights will be subject to institutional guidelines and policy. OTHER REQUIREMENTS: Prior to commencement of work described, all personnel will be required to obtain and maintain all appropriate certifications for performing preclinical research at the VA and MHMH/DHC, including CITI and Bioraft training, IACUC approval, and VA-Without Compensation (WOC) research affiliate designation. INTRODUCTION AND PURPOSE The primary objective of the Advanced Navigation Simulation Environment Laboratory (ANSEL) acquisition effort is to obtain comprehensive engineering, technical, and integration support to modernize the Position, Navigation, and Timing (PNT) and Navigation Warfare (NAVWAR) simulation capabilities within the Holloman AFB PNT Simulation Laboratory.
